thread.text:
Most arcade drifting games give you a magic "press space to drift" button.

We built a top-down driving engine where drifting relies entirely on realistic weight-transfer, throttle oversteer, and EV regen braking.

No handbrake. Pure physics. Runs instantly in your browser 🏎️⚡
thread.mediaNote: Crisp 6-8s looping gameplay GIF: EV tapping brakes, swinging into a wide oversteer drift around a snowy bend, kicking up powder, and boosting past oncoming traffic.

thread.text:
How the physics model works under the hood:

1. Brake before turn-in → dynamic weight shifts to front axle
2. Unloaded rear breaks traction → initiates oversteer
3. Throttle balances the yaw angle
4. Countersteer to catch the snap

Mess up the line? Off-road grass drains battery 90x faster.
thread.mediaNote: Diagram/split-screen overlay showing weight transfer vector lines and EV battery discharge rates during a turn.

thread.text:
Even the audio is synthesized in real time via WebAudio API:

• Motor whine pitch = wheel RPM
• Audio amplitude = instantaneous power (|kW|)
• Downward pitch-bend on kinetic regen braking

No MP3 asset files. Just pure procedural frequency synthesis running on the CPU.
thread.mediaNote: Short video clip with sound demonstrating the EV motor whine pitch shifting dynamically from heavy acceleration to regenerative braking.

thread.text:
The wild part? The entire game—physics engine, dual-view rendering, procedural biomes, zombie bounties, and deterministic daily ghost lines—lives inside a single index.html file.

0 npm packages. 0 build steps. Loads in under 0.1 seconds.
